items.q: سانحات کے اِنتظام سے کیا مراد ہے نیز اِس کیلئے منصوبہ سازی پر بحث کیجیے۔
items.q2: What is meant by disaster management? Also discuss planning for it.
items.q3: د ناورینونو له مدیریت څه مراد دی؟ د هغه لپاره پر پلان جوړونې هم بحث وکړئ.
items.a: آفات کا انتظام وہ عمل ہے جس میں کسی بڑے واقعے یا حادثے سے اس طرح نمٹا جائے کہ عوام اس کے نقصانات سے مکمل بچ جائیں یا نقصان کم سے کم ہو؛ خطرناک صورتحال کو بروقت سمجھنا، شناخت کرنا، درست تعین کرنا اور کم سے کم وقت میں فیصلہ کر کے نمٹنا۔ آفات کی اقسام: قدرتی (زلزلہ، آگ، سیلاب، طوفان، لینڈ سلائیڈنگ، وبا، عمارت کا گرنا) اور انسانی (شعوری — جنگ، دہشت گردی، دھماکے؛ غیر شعوری — ٹریفک حادثات)۔ منصوبہ بندی: بہترین انتظام خطرات کم کرنے کے ساتھ متاثرین کو بہتری کے زیادہ سے زیادہ مواقع دیتا ہے؛ یہ ایک فن ہے اور اس میں مشاہدے، مطالعے اور تجربے سے ماہر افراد کام کرتے ہیں؛ منصوبہ ایک دستاویزی پروگرام ہے جس میں سانحے کے دوران اور بعد کی تمام سرگرمیاں شامل ہیں۔ ٹیم کی سرگرمیاں: فوراً ذمہ داری اور مقام سنبھالنا، حقائق کا تعین، اپنا مؤقف بیان کرنا اور مسئلے پر قابو پانا؛ ہر رکن کا کردار طے؛ ذمہ دار لوگوں کی موجودگی تاکہ موقع پر احکامات اور رقم مل سکے؛ کیا، کب، کیوں، کہاں، کس کے لیے اور کون — کے جواب منصوبے میں ہوں۔ نعرہ "تیار رہنا": ہر قسم کے سانحے کی تیاری؛ کمیونٹی، سول ڈیفنس، این جی اوز اور رضاکاروں کی شمولیت؛ متاثرین کی بحالی کا منصوبہ۔
items.h: درج ذیل سوالات کے تفصیلی جواب لکھیں:

items.q: کمیونٹی سروس پر نوٹ لکھیں۔
items.q2: Write a note on community service.
items.q3: پر ټولنیز خدمت یادښت ولیکئ.
items.a: کمیونٹی سروس سے مراد عوامی خدمت یا عطیات پر مبنی سرگرمی ہے جس سے کمیونٹی کو فائدہ ہو؛ یہ عموماً رضاکاروں کا کام ہے، مگر بعض لوگ معاوضہ لیتے یا پابند کیے جاتے ہیں (بعض حکومتیں شہریوں پر لازمی کرتی ہیں؛ فوجی ملازمین اور سکولوں کے طلبہ تربیت کے طور پر)۔ ہر شہری کی اخلاقی ذمہ داری ہے کہ اپنی کمیونٹی کی خدمت کے لیے آگے آئے؛ صرف اپنا پیٹ بھرنا اچھی شہریت کے لیے کافی نہیں۔ مثالیں: بچوں کو پڑھانا، کم آمدنی والوں کے لیے سادہ مکانات بنانا، بزرگوں کی خدمت، جانوروں کے لیے پناہ گاہیں، آگ بجھانا، ہنگامی خدمات اور علاقے کی خوبصورتی (صفائی مہم، شجرکاری)۔ محرکات: آخرت کی کامیابی، اللہ کی رضا، حقیقی خوشی، اجتماعی زندگی میں سکون، انسانی خدمت کا جذبہ اور روحانی نجات؛ بعض کو سزا کے طور پر بھی لگایا جاتا ہے۔ فوائد: نئے لوگوں کو سیکھنے کا موقع، کمیونٹی کے مسائل کا ادراک، بہتر ماحول اور سماجی ہم آہنگی؛ اس کے فوائد ہی فوائد ہیں، نقصان کوئی نہیں۔
items.h: درج ذیل سوالات کے تفصیلی جواب لکھیں:

items.q: ٹی وی پر ایک عوامی خدمت کے اِعلان کی تیاری (مواد، آواز اور شکل کو مدِنظر رکھتے ہوئے)۔
items.q2: Preparing a public service announcement on TV (keeping material, voice and form in view).
items.q3: په ټلوېزیون د عامه خدمت د یوه اعلان چمتو کول (مواد، غږ او بڼه په پام کې نیولو سره).
items.a: نمونے کا جواب: (عوامی خدمت کا اعلان) موضوع مثلاً «صفائی نصف ایمان ہے» یا «ٹریفک قوانین کی پابندی»؛ مواد: ایک سادہ پیغام، ایک مسئلہ اور اس کا حل، 30 سیکنڈ کا دورانیہ؛ آواز: صاف، دوستانہ اور واضح لہجہ؛ شکل: بصری مناظر، تحریر اور رنگ، آخر میں نعرہ؛ تیاری: اسکرپٹ، ریہرسل، کیمرا یا موبائل سے ریکارڈنگ۔
items.e: عملی سرگرمی۔
items.h: درج ذیل سوالات کے تفصیلی جواب لکھیں:

items.q: کسی عالمی یا قومی مسئلہ پر دستخطی مہم چلانا۔
items.q2: Running a signature campaign on some world or national issue.
items.q3: پر یوې نړیوالې یا ملي مسئلې د لاسلیک کمپاین چلول.
items.a: نمونے کا جواب: (دستخطی مہم) مسئلہ چنیں (مثلاً تعلیم سب کے لیے، پلاسٹک کے استعمال کی کمی)؛ مطالبہ ایک جملے میں لکھیں؛ دستخط کا فارم بنائیں (نام، پتہ/شناخت، دستخط)؛ اسکول، محلے اور بازار میں اجازت لے کر دستخط جمع کریں؛ دستخط والا ریکارڈ متعلقہ ادارے یا حکام کو پیش کریں؛ مہم کی رپورٹ لکھیں۔

items.h: درج ذیل سوالات کے تفصیلی جواب لکھیں:

items.q: دستخطی مہم کیلئے انٹرنٹ کا اِستعمال تاکہ لوگ دستخط کریں۔
items.q2: Using the internet for a signature campaign so that people sign.
items.q3: د لاسلیک کمپاین لپاره د انټرنېټ کارول ترڅو خلک لاسلیک وکړي.
items.a: نمونے کا جواب: (آن لائن دستخطی مہم) کسی معتبر پلیٹ فارم (مثلاً Change.org یا ادارے کی ویب سائٹ) پر درخواست بنائیں؛ اس میں مسئلہ، مطالبہ اور مخاطب ادارہ لکھیں؛ لنک کو سوشل میڈیا اور واٹس ایپ پر پھیلائیں؛ لوگوں کو آسان طریقے سے دستخط کرنا بتائیں؛ ذاتی معلومات کی حفاظت کریں اور جعلی یا غیر معتبر ویب سائٹ سے بچیں؛ تعداد کا ریکارڈ رکھیں۔
items.e: عملی سرگرمی۔ اس میں استاد اور والدین کی نگرانی رکھیں۔
items.h: درج ذیل سوالات کے تفصیلی جواب لکھیں:

items.q: Operating system is an:
items.e: An operating system is system software: it manages hardware and provides services for application programs.
items.q2: آپریٹنگ سسٹم ہے: (a) ایپلیکیشن سافٹ ویئر (b) سسٹم سافٹ ویئر (c) ڈرائیور (d) ان میں سے کوئی نہیں
items.q3: عملیاتي سیسټم یو دی: (a) کاريال سافټویر (b) سیسټم سافټویر (c) چلوونکی (d) له پورته هېڅ یو

items.q: DOS stands for:
items.e: DOS stands for Disk Operating System (e.g. MS-DOS).

items.q: Which one of the following is correct for multiprocessing operating systems?
o: Used on systems having only one processor
Cannot execute more than one processes at a time
Run on systems which having more than one processors
items.e: A multiprocessing operating system runs on computers having more than one processor (CPU) and can execute several processes at the same time.
items.q2: ملٹی پروسیسنگ آپریٹنگ سسٹمز کے لیے درج ذیل میں سے کون سا درست ہے؟ (a) صرف ایک پروسیسر والے سسٹمز پر استعمال ہوتے ہیں (b) ایک وقت میں ایک سے زیادہ پراسیسز نہیں چلا سکتے (c) ایک سے زیادہ پروسیسر والے سسٹمز پر چلتے ہیں (d) ان میں سے کوئی نہیں
items.q3: د څو-پروسسي عملیاتي سیسټمونو لپاره له لاندې څخه کوم یو سم دی؟ (a) یوازې پر یو-پروسېسوري سیسټمونو کارول کېږي (b) په یو وخت له یوې زیاتې پروسې نه شي اجرا کولی (c) پر هغو سیسټمونو چلېږي چې له یوه زیات پروسېسرونه لري (d) له پورته هېڅ یو

items.q: Multiprogramming refers to:
o: Having several programs in RAM at the same time
items.e: Multiprogramming means keeping several programs in main memory (RAM) at the same time so that the CPU switches to another program when one waits for I/O.

items.q: The most recently launched operating system of Microsoft is:
items.e: Among the given choices Windows 8 is the most recent Microsoft operating system.

items.q: Which of the following is not an operating system?
items.e: MS Word is an application (word-processing) program, not an operating system; Linux, UNIX and Windows XP are operating systems.

items.q: Which type of software enables you to solve specific problems or perform specific tasks?
items.e: Application software is designed to solve specific problems or perform specific tasks for the user (word processing, accounting, games).
items.q2: کس قسم کا سافٹ ویئر آپ کو مخصوص مسائل حل کرنے یا مخصوص کام انجام دینے کے قابل بناتا ہے؟ (a) سسٹم سافٹ ویئر (b) آپریٹنگ سسٹم (c) یوٹیلیٹی سافٹ ویئر (d) ایپلیکیشن سافٹ ویئر
items.q3: کوم ډول سافټویر تاسو ته د ځانګړو ستونزو د حل یا ځانګړو دندو د ترسره کولو وړتیا درکوي؟ (a) سیسټم سافټویر (b) عملیاتي سیسټم (c) ګټور سافټویر (d) کاريال سافټویر

items.q: Which type of software controls your application software and manages how your hardware devices work together?
items.e: The operating system controls the application software and manages how the hardware devices work together. (It is a part of system software.)
items.q2: کس قسم کا سافٹ ویئر آپ کے ایپلیکیشن سافٹ ویئر کو کنٹرول کرتا ہے اور اس کا انتظام کرتا ہے کہ آپ کے ہارڈویئر آلات مل کر کیسے کام کریں؟ (a) سسٹم سافٹ ویئر (b) آپریٹنگ سسٹم (c) یوٹیلیٹی سافٹ ویئر (d) ایپلیکیشن سافٹ ویئر
items.q3: کوم ډول سافټویر ستاسو کاريال سافټویر کنټرولوي او اداره کوي چې ستاسو هارډویري وسایل څنګه یوځای کار وکړي؟ (a) سیسټم سافټویر (b) عملیاتي سیسټم (c) ګټور سافټویر (d) کاريال سافټویر

items.q: A technique in which a process, executing an application, is divided into threads that can run concurrently is called:
items.e: Multithreading divides a process into threads that can run concurrently.
items.q2: وہ تکنیک جس میں کسی ایپلیکیشن کو چلانے والا پراسیس ایسے تھریڈز میں تقسیم ہوتا ہے جو بیک وقت چل سکیں، کہلاتی ہے: (a) ملٹی تھریڈنگ (b) ملٹی پروسیسنگ (c) بیچ پراسیسنگ (d) ان میں سے کوئی نہیں
items.q3: هغه تخنیک چې پکې یو کاريال اجرا کوونکې پروسه په داسې تارونو وېشل کېږي چې په یو وخت چلېدای شي، بلل کېږي: (a) څو-تاریز کار (b) څو-پروسسي کار (c) ډله‌ییز پروسس (d) له پورته هېڅ یو

items.q: The operating system acts as an interface between the computer hardware and the human user.
items.e: True — the OS is the interface between the hardware and the user.
items.q2: آپریٹنگ سسٹم کمپیوٹر ہارڈویئر اور انسانی صارف کے درمیان انٹرفیس کا کام کرتا ہے۔
items.q3: عملیاتي سیسټم د کمپیوټري هارډویر او انساني کاروونکي ترمنځ د منځګړي کار کوي.

items.q: Multiprogramming allows the processor to make use of idle time caused by I/O wait.
items.e: True — while one program waits for I/O, the processor runs another program, using the idle time.
items.q2: ملٹی پروگرامنگ پروسیسر کو I/O انتظار سے پیدا ہونے والے فارغ وقت کو استعمال کرنے دیتی ہے۔
items.q3: څو-پروګرامي کار پروسېسر ته اجازه ورکوي چې د I/O انتظار له امله له وزګار وخت ګټه واخلي.

items.q: An operating system controls the execution of applications and acts as an interface between applications and the computer hardware.
items.e: True — the OS controls the execution of applications and acts as an interface between applications and hardware.
items.q2: آپریٹنگ سسٹم ایپلیکیشنز کے چلنے کو کنٹرول کرتا ہے اور ایپلیکیشنز اور کمپیوٹر ہارڈویئر کے درمیان انٹرفیس کا کام کرتا ہے۔
items.q3: عملیاتي سیسټم د کاريالونو اجرا کنټرولوي او د کاريالونو او کمپیوټري هارډویر ترمنځ د منځګړي کار کوي.

items.q: In the early computers, the operating systems did not exist.
items.e: True — the earliest computers had no operating system; programs were loaded and run manually.
items.q2: ابتدائی کمپیوٹرز میں آپریٹنگ سسٹم موجود نہیں تھے۔
items.q3: په لومړنیو کمپیوټرونو کې عملیاتي سیسټمونه نه وو.

items.q: Multi-programming do not provide better utilization of system resources than multiprogramming.
items.e: False — multiprogramming provides better utilisation of system resources (CPU and I/O) than uniprogramming.
items.q2: ملٹی پروگرامنگ، ملٹی پروگرامنگ کے مقابلے میں سسٹم کے وسائل کا بہتر استعمال فراہم نہیں کرتی۔
items.q3: څو-پروګرامي کار د څو-پروګرامي کار په پرتله د سیسټم د سرچینو ښه کارونه نه برابروي.

items.q: In a time sharing system, when a process is assigned to the CPU for execution, it remains there till its completion.
items.e: False — in a time-sharing system each process gets the CPU only for a short time slice (quantum) and then the CPU switches to another process.

items.q: A process is a dispatchable unit of thread.
items.e: False — a thread is the dispatchable unit of a process (a process contains one or more threads).
items.q2: پراسیس تھریڈ کی ایک قابلِ روانگی اکائی ہے۔
items.q3: پروسه د تار د لېږلو وړ واحد دی.

items.q: A process is directly assigned to the CPU for processing from a block state when the event for which it is waiting happens.
items.e: False — when the awaited event occurs, a blocked process moves to the ready state, not directly to the CPU (running).

items.q: A process is said to be in ready state if it is waiting for some external event which has not yet been occurred.
items.e: False — a process waiting for an external event is in the blocked (waiting) state; a ready process is waiting only for the CPU.
items.q2: پراسیس اس وقت تیار حالت میں کہلاتا ہے جب وہ کسی ایسے بیرونی واقعے کا انتظار کر رہا ہو جو ابھی پیش نہیں آیا۔
items.q3: یوه پروسه هغه وخت په چمتو حالت کې ګڼل کېږي چې د کومې بهرنۍ پېښې انتظار باسي چې لا نه ده پېښه شوې.

items.q: Batch processing systems does not support interactivity.
items.e: True — in batch processing jobs are collected and run without user interaction.

items.q: The first step in the system development life cycle is:
items.e: The first step of SDLC is problem identification (planning) — defining the problem and objectives.
items.q2: سسٹم ڈویلپمنٹ لائف سائیکل کا پہلا مرحلہ ہے: (a) تجزیہ (b) ڈیزائن (c) مسئلے کی نشاندہی (d) تیاری اور دستاویز بندی

items.e: The organised set of steps followed to develop an information system is the System Development Life Cycle.

items.q: Enhancements, upgradation and bugs fixation are done during the ________ step in the SDLC.
items.e: Enhancements, upgrades and bug fixes are done in the maintenance (and evaluation) phase.

items.q: The ________ determines whether the project should go forward.
items.e: The feasibility study determines whether the project should go forward (technical, economic, operational feasibility).
items.q2: ________ طے کرتا ہے کہ آیا منصوبہ آگے بڑھنا چاہیے۔ (a) فیزیبلٹی (b) مسئلے کی نشاندہی (c) نظام کا جائزہ (d) پروگرام کی تفصیل
items.q3: ________ ټاکي چې ایا پروژه دې مخ ته ولاړه شي. (a) د عملي کېدو وړتیا (b) د ستونزې پېژندنه (c) د سیسټم ارزونه (d) د پروګرام مشخصات

items.q: ________ spend most of their time in the beginning stages of the SDLC, talking with end-users, gathering requirements, documenting systems and proposing solutions.
items.e: System analysts spend most of their time in the early stages — meeting users, gathering requirements, documenting and proposing solutions.

items.q: The entities having a positive or negative influence in the project completion are known as ________ .
items.e: Stakeholders are the people/organisations who influence or are affected by the project.
items.q2: منصوبے کی تکمیل پر مثبت یا منفی اثر رکھنے والے ادارے ________ کہلاتے ہیں۔ (a) اسٹیک ہولڈرز (b) اسٹیک سپروائزرز (c) اسٹیک اونرز (d) ان میں سے کوئی نہیں

items.q: System maintenance is performed in response to ________ .
items.e: Maintenance is performed in response to business changes, hardware and software changes, and users' requests for new features.
items.q2: نظام کی دیکھ بھال ________ کے جواب میں کی جاتی ہے۔ (a) کاروباری تبدیلیوں (b) ہارڈویئر اور سافٹ ویئر کی تبدیلیوں (c) اضافی خصوصیات کے لیے صارف کی درخواستوں (d) مندرجہ بالا سب

items.q: A stakeholder is any person or organization who has a direct or indirect interest in the project.
items.e: True — a stakeholder is any person or organisation with a direct or indirect interest in the project.
items.q2: اسٹیک ہولڈر کوئی بھی شخص یا تنظیم ہے جو منصوبے میں براہِ راست یا بالواسطہ دلچسپی رکھتی ہو۔
items.q3: ښکېل اړخ هر هغه کس یا سازمان دی چې په پروژه کې مستقیمه یا غیر مستقیمه لېوالتیا لري.

items.q: System maintenance is performed to gather the requirements of the proposed system.
items.e: False — requirements are gathered in the analysis phase; maintenance is done after deployment to correct and improve the system.
items.q2: نظام کی دیکھ بھال مجوزہ نظام کی ضروریات جمع کرنے کے لیے کی جاتی ہے۔
items.q3: د سیسټم ساتنه د وړاندیز شوي سیسټم د اړتیاوو د راټولولو لپاره کېږي.

items.q: The how, when, what type of questions are answered in the planning phase of SDLC.
items.e: True — the planning phase answers what is to be done, how, when, by whom and at what cost.

items.q: The three architectures i.e. algorithms, pseudo code and flowcharts are used in the implementation phase of SDLC.
items.e: False — algorithms, pseudo code and flowcharts are used in the design phase, before implementation (coding).

items.q: Each phase of SDLC is accomplished as a discrete, separate step.
items.e: True — in the classical (waterfall) SDLC each phase is completed as a separate step before the next begins.

items.q: What does the given expression evaluate to? E=6 + 5 * 4 % 3
items.e: % and * have higher precedence than + and associate left to right: 5 * 4 = 20, 20 % 3 = 2, then 6 + 2 = 8.
items.q2: دیا گیا ایکسپریشن کس قدر کے برابر ہوگا؟ E=6 + 5 * 4 % 3 (a) 1 (b) 8 (c) 11 (d) ان میں سے کوئی نہیں
items.q3: ورکړل شوې افاده څه ارزښت ورکوي؟ E=6 + 5 * 4 % 3 (a) 1 (b) 8 (c) 11 (d) له پورته هېڅ یو

items.q: (true && true) || false
items.e: (true && true) = true; true || false = true.

items.q: Expression C=i++ causes
o: Value of i assigned to C and then i incremented by 1
i to be incremented by 1 and then value of i assigned to C
Value of i assigned to C
items.e: Post-increment: the current value of i is assigned to C first, then i is increased by 1.
items.q2: ایکسپریشن C=i++ کا نتیجہ (a) i کی قدر C کو تفویض ہوتی ہے اور پھر i میں 1 کا اضافہ ہوتا ہے (b) i میں 1 کا اضافہ اور پھر i کی قدر C کو تفویض (c) i کی قدر C کو تفویض (d) i میں 1 کا اضافہ

items.q: In C++ language char ch='3' represents:
items.e: '3' in single quotes is a character constant (ASCII value 51), not the integer 3.

items.q: Definition for the C++ object cout is stored in header file conio.h.
items.e: False — cout is defined in the header file iostream (iostream.h), not conio.h.

items.q: In C++ a statement ends with ':' symbol.
items.e: False — a C++ statement ends with a semicolon (;).
items.q2: C++ میں بیان ':' علامت پر ختم ہوتا ہے۔
items.q3: په C++ کې بیان د ':' نښې سره پای ته رسېږي.

items.q: int 20sum is the correct declaration of the variable 20sum.
items.e: False — a variable name cannot begin with a digit; 20sum is invalid (sum20 is valid).

items.q: In C++ the statement a=a+20 is the same as a+=20.
items.e: True — a += 20 is the compound assignment form of a = a + 20.
items.q2: C++ میں بیان a=a+20، a+=20 کے برابر ہے۔
items.q3: په C++ کې بیان a=a+20 له a+=20 سره یو شان دی.

items.q: Size of short int data type is 4 bytes.
items.e: False — short int usually occupies 2 bytes.

items.q: Looping in a program means
o: Jumping to the specified branch of program
Repeat the specified lines of code
items.e: Looping means repeating the specified lines of code a number of times or while a condition is true.
items.q2: پروگرام میں لوپنگ کا مطلب ہے (a) پروگرام کی مخصوص شاخ پر جانا (b) کوڈ کی مخصوص لائنیں دہرانا (c) دونوں (d) ان میں سے کوئی نہیں
items.q3: په پروګرام کې حلقه کول معنا لري (a) د پروګرام ټاکلې څانګې ته ټوپ (b) د کوډ ټاکلې کرښې تکرارول (c) دواړه پورته (d) له پورته هېڅ یو

items.q: Which of the following is not a looping statement in C++?
items.e: C++ has while, do-while and for loops; there is no 'until' loop.

items.q: The continue statement
o: resumes the program if it is hanged
resumes the program if break was applied
skips the rest of the loop in current iteration
items.e: continue skips the remaining statements of the loop body in the current iteration and starts the next iteration.

items.q: Decision-making structures cannot be nested.
items.e: False — decision-making structures can be nested (an if inside another if or switch).
items.q2: فیصلہ سازی کی ساختیں نیسٹ نہیں کی جا سکتیں۔
items.q3: پرېکړه‌ییز جوړښتونه ځالې کېدای نه شي.

items.q: Body of do while loop is executed at least once if the condition is false.
items.e: True — do-while checks its condition after the body, so the body runs at least once even if the condition is false.

items.q: switch statement is a better alternative of nested if-else structure.
items.e: True — when one variable is compared with many constant values, switch is clearer than a long nested if-else chain.

items.q: Syntax of if-else statement is:
items.e: False — the correct syntax is: if (condition) { statements } else { statements }; else must come after the if block.

items.q: A collection of data items of the same data types placed in contiguous memory locations is called ________ .
items.e: An array is a collection of items of the same data type stored in contiguous memory locations.
items.q2: متصل میموری مقامات میں رکھے گئے ایک ہی ڈیٹا ٹائپ کے ڈیٹا آئٹمز کا مجموعہ ________ کہلاتا ہے۔ (a) ریکارڈ (b) ایرے (c) پروگرام (d) فائل
items.q3: په پرله‌پسې حافظه ځایونو کې د ایښودل شویو یو ډول ډېټا توکو ټولګه ________ بلل کېږي. (a) ریکارډ (b) لړۍ (c) پروګرام (d) دوتنه

items.q: The location number of an item in an array is called ________ .
items.e: The position number of an element in an array is its index (subscript).
items.q2: ایرے میں کسی آئٹم کے مقام کا نمبر ________ کہلاتا ہے۔ (a) ڈیٹا (b) قدر (c) انڈیکس (d) مستقل
items.q3: په لړۍ کې د یوه توکي د ځای شمېره ________ بلل کېږي. (a) ډېټا (b) ارزښت (c) شاخص (d) ثابت

items.q: Strings are character arrays. The last index of it contains the null character ________ .
items.e: A C-string ends with the null character '\0'.

items.q: Array is a collection of heterogeneous type of data.
items.e: False — an array is a collection of homogeneous data (all elements of the same type).
items.q2: ایرے مختلف النوع ڈیٹا کا مجموعہ ہے۔
items.q3: لړۍ د ناورته ډول ډېټا ټولګه ده.

items.q: Array can be initialized during declaration time.
items.e: True — e.g. int a[3] = {1, 2, 3}; initializes the array at declaration time.
items.q2: ایرے کو ڈکلیریشن کے وقت ابتدائی قدر دی جا سکتی ہے۔
items.q3: لړۍ ته د اعلان پر مهال لومړنی ارزښت ورکول کېدای شي.

items.q: char vowel[5] declares an integer type array that holds the vowel characters of English language.
items.e: False — char vowel[5] declares a character-type array, not an integer array.

items.q: Loop is the best tool for handling large arrays.
items.e: True — loops (especially for loops) are the best tool to process every element of a large array using the index.
items.q2: بڑے ایریز کو سنبھالنے کے لیے لوپ بہترین ذریعہ ہے۔
items.q3: د لویو لړیو د چلولو لپاره حلقه غوره وسیله ده.

items.q: Array elements are stored in the memory where ever free space is available.
items.e: False — array elements are stored in contiguous (adjacent) memory locations, not wherever free space is available.
items.q2: ایرے کے عناصر میموری میں جہاں بھی خالی جگہ دستیاب ہو، محفوظ ہوتے ہیں۔
items.q3: د لړۍ عناصر په حافظه کې هر چېرې چې تش ځای وي، ساتل کېږي.

items.q: The phenomenon of having two or more functions in a program with the same names but different number and types of parameters is known as:
items.e: Functions with the same name but a different number or types of parameters are overloaded functions — function overloading.
items.q2: کسی پروگرام میں ایک ہی نام لیکن مختلف تعداد اور اقسام کے پیرامیٹرز والے دو یا زیادہ فنکشنز ہونے کا عمل کہلاتا ہے: (a) ان لائن فنکشن (b) نیسٹڈ فنکشن (c) فنکشن اوورلوڈنگ (d) ریکرسیو فنکشن

items.q: We declare a function with ________ if it does not have any return type
items.e: A function that returns no value is declared with the return type void.

items.q: Arguments of a functions are separated with ________ .
items.e: Arguments (parameters) of a function are separated by commas, e.g. sum(int a, int b).
items.q2: فنکشن کے آرگیومنٹس ________ سے الگ کیے جاتے ہیں۔ (a) کاما (,) (b) سیمی کولن (;) (c) کولن (:) (d) ان میں سے کوئی نہیں
items.q3: د فنکشن دلیلونه په ________ جلا کېږي. (a) کامه (,) (b) سیمي‌کولن (;) (c) کولن (:) (d) له دې هېڅ یو

items.q: Variables inside parenthesis of functions declarations have ________ level access.
items.e: Parameters declared inside the parentheses are local to that function.
items.q2: فنکشنز کی ڈکلیریشنز کی قوسین کے اندر ویری ایبلز کی رسائی ________ سطح کی ہوتی ہے۔ (a) مقامی (b) عالمی (c) ماڈیول (d) آفاقی
items.q3: د فنکشنونو د اعلانونو د قوسونو دننه متغیرونه د ________ کچې لاسرسی لري. (a) محلي (b) نړیوال (c) ماډیول (d) نړیوال‌شمول

items.q: A function cannot be overloaded only by its return type.
items.e: True — functions that differ only in return type cannot be overloaded; the parameter list must differ.
items.q2: فنکشن کو صرف اس کی ریٹرن ٹائپ سے اوورلوڈ نہیں کیا جا سکتا۔
items.q3: فنکشن یوازې د بېرته ورکړې په ډول نه شي ډېرېدای.

items.q: A function can be overloaded with a different return type if it has all the parameters same.
items.e: False — if all the parameters are the same, changing only the return type does not overload the function; it is a compile error.
items.q2: اگر فنکشن کے تمام پیرامیٹرز ایک جیسے ہوں تو اسے مختلف ریٹرن ٹائپ کے ساتھ اوورلوڈ کیا جا سکتا ہے۔
items.q3: که د فنکشن ټول پاراميټرونه ورته وي، د بېل د بېرته ورکړې ډول سره ډېرېدای شي.

items.q: Inline functions minimize the size of the program.
items.e: False — inline functions are expanded wherever they are called, which usually increases program size but saves the time of function calls.
items.q2: ان لائن فنکشنز پروگرام کا سائز کم کرتے ہیں۔

items.q: If we have a function: int sum (int x, int y), then it will return float value to the calling program.
items.e: False — int sum(int x, int y) returns an int value.

items.q: Passing arguments by address allows the function to change the value of the argument.
items.e: True — when the address is passed (pointer/reference), the function works on the original variable and can change it.
items.q2: پتے کے ذریعے آرگیومنٹس پاس کرنا فنکشن کو آرگیومنٹ کی قدر تبدیل کرنے کی اجازت دیتا ہے۔
items.q3: د پتې له لارې د دلیلونو لېږدول فنکشن ته اجازه ورکوي چې د دلیل ارزښت بدل کړي.

items.q: If we have the statement int *Ptr; then to what Ptr point?
o: Points to an integer type variable
Points to a character type variable
Points to a floating point type variable
items.e: int *Ptr; declares Ptr as a pointer to an integer type variable.

items.q: A pointer is:
o: A keyword used to create variables
A variable that stores address of an instruction
A variable that stores address of another variable
items.e: A pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another variable.
items.q2: پوائنٹر ہے: (a) ویری ایبلز بنانے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا کلیدی لفظ (b) ایک ویری ایبل جو کسی ہدایت کا پتہ محفوظ کرتا ہے (c) ایک ویری ایبل جو دوسرے ویری ایبل کا پتہ محفوظ کرتا ہے (d) مندرجہ بالا سب
items.q3: پوائنټر دی: (a) د متغیرونو د جوړولو لپاره کارېدونکې کلیدي کلمه (b) هغه متغیر چې د یوې لارښوونې پته ساتي (c) هغه متغیر چې د بل متغیر پته ساتي (d) پورته ټول

items.q: In pointers, dereference operator * is used to:
o: Address the value of the pointer variable.
Points to the value stored in the variable pointed by the pointer variable
items.e: *ptr refers to the value stored in the variable that the pointer points to.
items.q2: پوائنٹرز میں ڈی ریفرنس آپریٹر * استعمال ہوتا ہے: (a) پوائنٹر ویری ایبل کی قدر کا پتہ دینے کے لیے (b) پوائنٹر ویری ایبل کی طرف سے اشارہ کردہ ویری ایبل میں محفوظ قدر کی طرف اشارہ کرنے کے لیے (c) a اور b دونوں (d) ان میں سے کوئی نہیں
items.q3: په پوائنټرونو کې د حوالې‌لرې کولو چلونکی * کارېږي: (a) د پوائنټر متغیر ارزښت ته پته ورکولو لپاره (b) هغه ارزښت ته اشاره چې د پوائنټر متغیر په اشاره شوي متغیر کې ساتل شوی (c) a او b دواړه (d) له پورته هېڅ یو

items.q: The statement int *ptr; defines an ordinary C++ variable.
items.e: False — int *ptr; defines a pointer variable that holds the address of an int, not an ordinary variable.

items.q: The following lines of codes assign the value of the variable Temp to the pointer variable PTemp.
items.e: False — the code assigns the address of Temp (&Temp) to PTemp, not the value of Temp.

items.q: Pointer variables can be initialized by addresses of the variables to which they refer.
items.e: True — e.g. int x; int *p = &x; initializes the pointer with the address of x.
items.q2: پوائنٹر ویری ایبلز کو ان ویری ایبلز کے پتوں سے ابتدائی قدر دی جا سکتی ہے جن کی طرف وہ اشارہ کرتے ہیں۔
items.q3: د پوائنټر متغیرونو ته د هغو متغیرونو پتې لومړنی ارزښت ورکول کېدای شي چې ورته اشاره کوي.

items.q: To assign addresses to pointers, a programmer needs a special type of operator called address-of-operator &.
items.e: True — the address-of operator & is used to obtain the address that is assigned to a pointer.

items.q: نجی مالیات اور سرکاری مالیات میں فرق بیان کیجئے؟ (سرگودھا بورڈ 2009ء، لاہور بورڈ 2010ء)
items.q2: State the difference between private finance and public finance. (Sargodha Board 2009, Lahore Board 2010)
items.q3: د خصوصي مالیې او دولتي مالیې توپیر بیان کړئ. (سرګودها بورډ ۲۰۰۹، لاهور بورډ ۲۰۱۰)
items.a: Private finance is the income and expenditure of individuals and firms; public finance is the income, expenditure and borrowing of the government. Differences: (1) Adjustment — an individual adjusts expenditure to his income, while the government first decides expenditure and then raises income. (2) Objective — private finance aims at personal satisfaction or profit; public finance aims at public welfare. (3) Sources — individuals earn from work and property; government gets taxes, fees, loans and can print notes. (4) Borrowing — the government can borrow internally and externally on a large scale; individuals have limited credit. (5) Secrecy — private budgets are kept secret, while the government budget is published and debated in parliament. (6) Time period — individuals plan for the short term; government plans for long periods (five-year plans). (7) Compulsion — government can collect taxes by law; individuals cannot force anyone to pay them. (8) Surplus — a surplus is good for an individual, but a surplus budget is not always good for a government.

items.q: ٹیکس عائد کرنے کے اصول بیان کریں؟ (ملتان بورڈ 2009ء، سرگودھا بورڈ 2010ء)
items.q2: State the principles of imposing tax. (Multan Board 2009, Sargodha Board 2010)
items.q3: د مالیې د لګولو اصول بیان کړئ. (ملتان بورډ ۲۰۰۹، سرګودها بورډ ۲۰۱۰)
items.a: Adam Smith's canons: (1) Equality — tax according to ability to pay; (2) Certainty — the amount, time and method of payment should be clear; (3) Convenience — tax should be collected at a time and in a way convenient for the taxpayer (e.g. tax deducted from salary); (4) Economy — cost of collection should be low. Other principles: (5) Productivity — the tax should yield enough revenue; (6) Elasticity — revenue should rise with need, e.g. by changing rates; (7) Flexibility — the system can be changed easily; (8) Simplicity — easy to understand; (9) Diversity — many kinds of taxes so the burden is spread; (10) Economic growth — taxes should not discourage saving, investment and production.

items.q: ٹیکسوں کی مختلف اقسام کی وضاحت کریں؟ (بہاولپور بورڈ 2010ء)
items.q2: Explain the different kinds of taxes. (Bahawalpur Board 2010)
items.q3: د مالیو بېلابېل ډولونه روښانه کړئ. (بهاولپور بورډ ۲۰۱۰)
items.a: Direct taxes — the burden falls on the person who pays them and cannot be shifted: income tax, wealth tax, property tax, corporation tax, capital gains tax. Indirect taxes — paid first by producers or traders but shifted to consumers through prices: sales tax, excise duty, customs (import/export) duties, value-added tax. By rate: Proportional tax — the same rate on all incomes; Progressive tax — the rate rises as income rises (income tax); Regressive tax — the rate falls as income rises, or it takes a larger share from the poor (many indirect taxes); Degressive tax — progressive up to a limit and then proportional. Other kinds: specific tax (per unit of goods) and ad valorem tax (as a percentage of value); single and multiple tax systems.

items.q: حکومت کے مختلف ذرائع آمدنی کی تفصیل بتایئے؟
items.q2: Give the detail of the different sources of income of the government.
items.q3: د حکومت د عاید د بېلابېلو سرچینو تفصیل ووایاست.
items.a: Tax revenue: income tax, corporation tax, wealth tax, property tax, sales tax/GST, central excise duty, customs duties on imports and exports, capital value tax. Non-tax revenue: fees (licence, court and registration fees), fines and penalties, prices of government services (railway, post, PTCL), profits of public enterprises (State Bank, WAPDA), interest on loans given to provinces, gifts and grants, escheats. Borrowing and others: internal loans (bonds, savings certificates, treasury bills), external loans and aid (IMF, World Bank, ADB, friendly countries), and deficit financing (borrowing from the central bank/printing notes). Provinces also get their share from the divisible pool under the NFC Award, land revenue, abiana (water rate), excise and stamp duties.

items.q: بالواسطہ ٹیکس کے فوائد اور نقصانات بیان کریں؟ (سرگودھا بورڈ 2011ء)
items.q2: State the benefits and harms of indirect tax. (Sargodha Board 2011)
items.q3: د غیر مستقیمې مالیې ګټې او زیانونه بیان کړئ. (سرګودها بورډ ۲۰۱۱)
items.a: Benefits of indirect tax: (1) Convenient — paid in small amounts when buying goods; (2) Difficult to evade, as it is included in prices; (3) Everyone, including the poor, contributes to state revenue; (4) Elastic — revenue rises as consumption increases; (5) Can discourage harmful goods (tobacco, alcohol) and luxury imports; (6) Cheap to collect from a few producers and importers. Harms: (1) Regressive — the poor pay a larger share of their income; (2) Uncertain — revenue depends on sales; (3) Raises prices and can cause inflation; (4) Reduces demand and may harm industry; (5) No civic consciousness, as people do not realise they pay tax; (6) Can encourage smuggling.

items.q: براہِ راست ٹیکس کی خوبیوں اور خامیوں پر بحث کریں؟ (بہاولپور بورڈ 2011ء، میرپور آزاد کشمیر بورڈ 2011ء)
items.q2: Discuss the merits and demerits of direct tax. (Bahawalpur Board 2011, Mirpur Azad Kashmir Board 2011)
items.q3: د مستقیمې مالیې پر ښېګڼو او نیمګړتیاوو بحث وکړئ. (بهاولپور بورډ ۲۰۱۱، میرپور آزاد کشمیر بورډ ۲۰۱۱)
items.a: Merits of direct tax: (1) Equitable — based on ability to pay and usually progressive; (2) Certain — taxpayer knows how much and when to pay; (3) Economical to collect; (4) Elastic and productive — revenue rises with income; (5) Creates civic consciousness; (6) Reduces inequalities of income and wealth. Demerits: (1) Inconvenient — paid in a lump sum; (2) Encourages evasion through false returns; (3) May discourage saving, investment and hard work if rates are high; (4) Arbitrary — rates are set by the government; (5) Narrow base in poor countries, since few people have taxable incomes; (6) Complicated assessment procedures.

items.q: پاکستان کے نظامِ محصولات کا جائزہ لیجئے؟ (لاہور بورڈ 2011ء)
items.q2: Review the tax system of Pakistan. (Lahore Board 2011)
items.q3: د پاکستان د مالیاتي نظام کتنه وکړئ. (لاهور بورډ ۲۰۱۱)
items.a: Features of Pakistan's tax system: (1) Narrow tax base — only a small percentage of people file income-tax returns; (2) Heavy dependence on indirect taxes (about two-thirds of revenue), making the system regressive; (3) Low tax-to-GDP ratio (around 9–11%); (4) Agricultural income is largely untaxed at the federal level. (5) Widespread tax evasion and a large undocumented economy; (6) Complicated laws and frequent changes; (7) Weak and sometimes corrupt tax administration; (8) Many exemptions and concessions; (9) Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) collects federal taxes, provinces collect their own taxes and get shares under the NFC Award; (10) Reforms such as GST, withholding taxes and computerisation have been introduced.

items.q: پاکستان میں نظامِ محصولات بہتر بنانے کے لیے تجاویز پیش کریں؟
items.q2: Present proposals to improve the tax system in Pakistan.
items.q3: په پاکستان کې د مالیاتي نظام د ښه کولو وړاندیزونه وړاندې کړئ.
items.a: (1) Broaden the tax base — bring all persons with taxable income, including big landlords and traders, into the tax net; (2) Reduce reliance on indirect taxes and increase the share of direct taxes; (3) Simplify tax laws and procedures and make them stable. (4) Reduce tax rates but enforce them strictly; (5) Remove unnecessary exemptions; (6) Computerise records, link NADRA, banks and property data to identify tax evaders; (7) Train honest tax officials and punish corruption; (8) Document the economy and encourage banking transactions. (9) Develop a tax culture through awareness and by spending tax money visibly on public welfare; (10) Tax agricultural income fairly; (11) Self-assessment schemes and easy online filing; (12) Coordinate federal and provincial taxes to avoid double taxation.

items.q: بین الاقوامی تجارت کے تقابلی مصارف کی برتری کے نظریہ کی تشریح کیجئے۔ (گوجرانوالہ بورڈ 2009ء)
items.q2: Explain the theory of comparative advantage in costs in international trade. (Gujranwala Board 2009)
items.q3: د نړیوالې سوداګرۍ د پرتلیزو لګښتونو د برترۍ نظریه تشریح کړئ. (ګوجرانواله بورډ ۲۰۰۹)
items.a: The theory of comparative advantage (comparative costs) was given by David Ricardo. It says that a country should specialise in producing those goods in which its comparative (relative) cost advantage is greatest, or comparative disadvantage least, and import the others; then both countries gain from trade even if one is more efficient in producing both goods. Assumptions: two countries, two goods; labour is the only factor; perfect competition; labour mobile within a country but not between countries; constant cost; no transport costs; full employment. Example: In Pakistan 10 days of labour produce 1 unit of cloth and 20 days 1 unit of wheat; in England 8 days produce cloth and 10 days produce wheat. England is better in both, but its advantage is greater in wheat (10/20 = 0.5) than in cloth (8/10 = 0.8). So England specialises in wheat, Pakistan in cloth (its disadvantage is least there), and by exchanging, both countries obtain more of both goods than without trade.

items.q: بین الاقوامی تجارت کے فوائد اور نقصانات بیان کیجئے۔ (لاہور بورڈ 2011ء، سرگودھا بورڈ 2010ء)
items.q2: State the benefits and harms of international trade. (Lahore Board 2011, Sargodha Board 2010)
items.q3: د نړیوالې سوداګرۍ ګټې او زیانونه بیان کړئ. (لاهور بورډ ۲۰۱۱، سرګودها بورډ ۲۰۱۰)
items.a: Benefits: specialisation and higher world production; availability of goods not produced at home; cheaper and better goods; wider markets for surplus output; foreign exchange earnings; transfer of technology; employment; help in emergencies; friendly international relations. Harms: (1) Dependence on other countries for necessities and defence goods, dangerous in war; (2) Competition from foreign goods can ruin infant domestic industries; (3) Exhaustion of natural resources through excessive exports of raw materials; (4) Import of harmful and luxury goods. (5) Spread of economic depression and inflation from one country to another; (6) Balance of payments deficits; (7) Exploitation of poor countries by rich nations and multinationals; (8) Under-developed countries remain producers of primary goods; (9) Cultural influence and political pressure.

items.q: نظریہ تقابلی مصارف کی تعریف کریں اور وضاحت بھی کریں۔ (بہاولپور بورڈ 2010ء، سرگودھا بورڈ 2011ء)
items.q2: Define the theory of comparative costs and also explain it. (Bahawalpur Board 2010, Sargodha Board 2011)
items.q3: د پرتلیزو لګښتونو نظریه تعریف کړئ او وضاحت یې هم وکړئ. (بهاولپور بورډ ۲۰۱۰، سرګودها بورډ ۲۰۱۱)
items.a: Definition: Ricardo's theory of comparative costs states that international trade takes place because of differences in comparative (relative) costs of producing goods in different countries; each country should produce and export the goods in which it has a comparative advantage and import those in which it has a comparative disadvantage. Explanation with a table (labour days for one unit): Country A — wheat 10, cloth 20; Country B — wheat 12, cloth 15. A has an absolute advantage in wheat, B in cloth. Comparative cost of wheat in terms of cloth: A = 0.5, B = 0.8, so A specialises in wheat; cloth: A = 2, B = 1.25, so B specialises in cloth. Gain from trade: if they exchange 1 wheat for (say) 1 cloth at a rate between their domestic cost ratios, A gets cloth for 10 days' labour instead of 20, and B gets wheat for 15 days instead of 12×… less than it would cost; total output of both goods rises. The theory holds even when one country is more efficient in both goods, as long as the cost ratios differ.

items.q2: Present a critical review of the theory of comparative costs.
items.q3: د پرتلیزو لګښتونو د نظریې انتقادي کتنه وړاندې کړئ.
items.a: Criticism: (1) Labour theory of value — it considers only labour as the cost, while capital, land and entrepreneurship also matter (Ohlin, Haberler); (2) Unrealistic assumption of only two countries and two goods; (3) Ignores transport costs, which can cancel the cost advantage; (4) Assumes constant costs, but in reality there are increasing and decreasing returns. (5) Assumes full employment and perfect competition, which do not exist; (6) Ignores demand — it does not tell the rate at which goods will be exchanged (J. S. Mill added reciprocal demand); (7) Assumes factors immobile between countries, but capital and labour do move; (8) Ignores tariffs, quotas and government policies; (9) Static theory — ignores changes in technology and growth; (10) Developing countries specialising in primary goods may lose from trade (terms of trade decline). Despite this, the theory explains the basic cause of trade.

items.q: گلوبلائزیشن سے کیا مراد ہے؟ اس کے فوائد بیان کیجئے۔
items.q2: What is meant by globalization? State its benefits.
items.q3: له ګلوبلایزېشن څه مراد دی؟ ګټې یې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Globalization is the process of integration of national economies into one world economy through free flow of trade, capital, technology, information and people, supported by the WTO and modern communication. Benefits: (1) Expansion of trade and markets; (2) Foreign direct investment and multinational companies bring capital and jobs; (3) Transfer of modern technology and management skills; (4) Consumers get cheaper, better and varied goods; (5) Competition increases efficiency and quality. (6) Information technology connects the world (internet, e-commerce); (7) Specialisation and economies of scale; (8) Growth of services such as banking, tourism and outsourcing; (9) Cultural exchange and international cooperation; (10) Faster economic growth for countries that can compete.

items.q: کثیر القومی کمپنیوں کے فوائد اور نقصانات پر بحث کریں۔
items.q2: Discuss the benefits and harms of multinational companies.
items.q3: د څو ملیتي شرکتونو پر ګټو او زیانونو بحث وکړئ.
items.a: A multinational company (MNC) is a business with its head office in one country and branches, factories or subsidiaries in many countries, e.g. Nestlé, Unilever, Coca-Cola, Toyota. Benefits: (1) Bring foreign capital and investment; (2) Transfer of modern technology and management; (3) Create employment and train local workers; (4) Increase production and exports, earning foreign exchange; (5) Pay taxes to the government; (6) Provide quality goods to consumers; (7) Develop local suppliers and industries. Harms: (1) Transfer large profits abroad, draining foreign exchange; (2) Destroy local small industries through competition; (3) Create monopolies and exploit consumers; (4) Use outdated or capital-intensive technology; (5) Exploit natural resources and cheap labour; (6) Influence the politics and policies of host countries; (7) Promote foreign culture and luxury consumption.

items.q: عالمی تجارتی تنظیم (WTO) کے اصول و قواعد اور کارکردگی بیان کیجئے۔
items.q2: State the principles, rules and performance of the World Trade Organization (WTO).
items.q3: د سوداګرۍ د نړیوال سازمان (WTO) اصول، قواعد او کارکړنه بیان کړئ.
items.a: The World Trade Organization (WTO) was established on 1 January 1995 in place of GATT; its headquarters is in Geneva and it has over 160 members, including Pakistan. Principles: (1) Non-discrimination — Most-Favoured-Nation treatment (equal treatment of all members) and national treatment (imported goods treated like local goods); (2) Freer trade — reduction of tariffs and removal of quotas; (3) Predictability — binding commitments and transparency; (4) Fair competition — rules against dumping and subsidies; (5) Special concessions for developing countries. Rules/agreements: GATT for goods, GATS for services, TRIPS for intellectual property, TRIMs for investment, Agreement on Agriculture, Agreement on Textiles and Clothing (quotas ended 2005), anti-dumping and dispute-settlement rules. Performance: it has reduced tariffs and expanded world trade, settled hundreds of trade disputes, given a forum for trade negotiations (Doha Round), and helped integrate developing countries; but it is criticised because rich countries still protect agriculture, and poor countries' industries face strong competition.

items.q: پاکستان میں معیارِ زندگی پست ہونے کے اسباب بیان کیجیے۔ (لاہور بورڈ 2009ء)

items.a: (1) Low per capita income; (2) Rapid population growth — large families with few earners; (3) Unemployment and disguised unemployment; (4) Inflation — rising prices reduce real income; (5) Unequal distribution of income and wealth. (6) Low productivity of agriculture and industry; (7) Illiteracy and lack of technical skills; (8) Poor health facilities and nutrition; (9) Shortage of capital and low saving and investment; (10) Shortage of energy (electricity, gas). (11) Political instability, corruption and bad governance; (12) Heavy burden of foreign debt; (13) Social evils — extravagance on ceremonies, dowry; (14) Under-utilisation of natural resources; (15) Inadequate infrastructure and housing.

items.q: پاکستان میں فی کس آمدنی کی کمی کے اسباب تحریر کیجیے۔ (ملتان بورڈ 2009ء، لاہور بورڈ 2010ء)

items.q3: په پاکستان کې د سړي سر عاید د کمښت لاملونه ولیکئ. (ملتان بورډ ۲۰۰۹، لاهور بورډ ۲۰۱۰)
items.a: (1) Rapid growth of population (about 2% a year) divides national income among more people; (2) Low productivity in agriculture due to old methods, small holdings and shortage of water; (3) Slow industrial growth; (4) Shortage of capital — low savings and investment. (5) Illiteracy and lack of technical education reduce efficiency of labour; (6) Unemployment and disguised unemployment; (7) Under-utilisation of natural resources; (8) Energy shortages; (9) Unequal distribution of wealth — feudal system and concentration in few hands. (10) Political instability and law-and-order problems discourage investment; (11) Heavy defence expenditure and debt servicing; (12) Inflation; (13) Corruption and inefficient administration; (14) Natural disasters such as floods and droughts.
items.h: صنعتی شعبہ کے مسائل کا حل لکھیں۔

items.q: پاکستان کی فی کس آمدنی پست ہونے کی وجوہات تحریر کریں۔ (ملتان بورڈ 2011ء)
items.q2: Write the reasons for Pakistan’s per capita income being low. (Multan Board 2011)
items.q3: د پاکستان د سړي سر عاید د ټیټوالي لاملونه ولیکئ. (ملتان بورډ ۲۰۱۱)
items.a: The reasons are: high population growth rate; dependence on backward agriculture; small and slowly growing industrial base; shortage of capital and technology; low literacy and skills; unemployment; underdeveloped natural resources; shortage of electricity and gas. Also: unequal distribution of income (landlords and industrialists hold most wealth); corruption and bad governance; political instability; heavy foreign debt and defence burden; inflation; low exports and trade deficit; social customs causing wasteful spending; and natural calamities.
items.h: صنعتی شعبہ کے مسائل کا حل لکھیں۔

items.q: پاکستان کی قومی آمدنی میں اضافہ کس طرح کیا جا سکتا ہے؟
items.q2: How can an increase be made in the national income of Pakistan?
items.q3: د پاکستان په ملي عاید کې څنګه زیاتوالی راتلی شي؟
items.a: (1) Control population growth through family planning and education; (2) Modernise agriculture — improved seeds, fertilisers, machinery, irrigation and credit; (3) Rapid industrialisation, especially agro-based and small industries; (4) Increase saving and investment; encourage foreign investment. (5) Develop human resources — education, technical training and health; (6) Overcome energy shortages by building dams and using alternative energy; (7) Exploit natural resources (minerals, gas, coal); (8) Increase exports and reduce unnecessary imports. (9) Political stability and good law and order; (10) Remove corruption and improve governance; (11) Fair distribution of wealth through land reforms and progressive taxation; (12) Economic planning; (13) Enforcement of the Islamic economic system (zakat, ushr, interest-free economy); (14) Develop infrastructure — roads, communications, IT.

items.a: Economic factors: (1) Natural resources — land, minerals, water, forests; (2) Capital formation — saving and investment; (3) Human resources — educated, skilled and healthy labour; (4) Technology and innovation; (5) Entrepreneurship; (6) Infrastructure — transport, communications, energy; (7) Size of the market and foreign trade. Non-economic factors: (1) Political stability and good governance; (2) Law and order; (3) Social values — honesty, hard work, absence of social evils; (4) Education and attitudes towards change; (5) Sound institutions (banks, courts); (6) Population control; (7) Economic planning and sound government policies; (8) International cooperation, aid and peace.

items.a: (1) Shortage of energy — load-shedding of electricity and gas; (2) Shortage of capital and high interest rates; (3) Outdated machinery and lack of modern technology; (4) Shortage of skilled labour and managers; (5) Dependence on imported raw materials and machinery. (6) Political instability and inconsistent industrial policies; (7) Law-and-order problems and labour disputes; (8) High taxes and complicated procedures; (9) Limited domestic market and competition from foreign (smuggled) goods; (10) Lack of research and development. (11) Concentration on a few industries (textiles); (12) Sick units and poor management; (13) Inadequate infrastructure; (14) Corruption and red tape; (15) Under-utilisation of installed capacity.

items.a: Importance and benefits of economic planning: (1) Efficient use of limited resources according to national priorities; (2) Rapid economic growth and increase in national and per capita income; (3) Removal of unemployment; (4) Balanced development of all sectors and regions. (5) Reduction in inequalities of income and wealth; (6) Development of infrastructure (dams, roads, power); (7) Industrialisation and modernisation of agriculture; (8) Price stability and control of inflation; (9) Mobilisation of savings and capital formation. (10) Improvement of social services — education, health, housing; (11) Self-reliance — less dependence on foreign aid; (12) Improvement in balance of payments; (13) Coordination between public and private sectors; (14) Achievement of a welfare state.

items.a: (1) Increase national and per capita income through a high growth rate; (2) Provide employment opportunities and reduce poverty; (3) Increase agricultural production and achieve self-sufficiency in food; (4) Rapid industrialisation; (5) Develop human resources — literacy, technical education and health. (6) Develop energy resources and infrastructure; (7) Reduce income inequality and regional imbalances; (8) Control population growth; (9) Increase exports and reduce the trade deficit; (10) Control inflation and keep prices stable; (11) Reduce dependence on foreign loans; (12) Improve housing, water supply and the environment; (13) Promote science and IT; (14) Establish an Islamic welfare state.

items.a: Means of communications (post, telephone, mobile, internet, radio, TV) and transport (roads, railways, airways, shipping, pipelines) are the backbone of an economy. Importance: (1) Expansion of markets — goods reach distant markets; (2) Development of agriculture — inputs reach farms and crops reach markets quickly; (3) Industrial growth — raw materials and finished goods are moved cheaply; (4) Large-scale production and division of labour; (5) Mobility of labour and capital. (6) Price stability — goods move from surplus to deficit areas; (7) Growth of trade, both internal and foreign; (8) Employment in transport and telecom sectors; (9) Defence and national integration; (10) Spread of education, culture and information; (11) Help in emergencies and natural disasters; (12) Development of tourism and backward areas.

items.q: پاکستان ریلوے کی اہمیت اور کارکردگی پر نوٹ لکھیں۔
items.q2: Write a note on the importance and performance of Pakistan Railway.
items.q3: د پاکستان رېل پر اهمیت او کارکړنې یادښت ولیکئ.
items.a: Pakistan Railways is the national railway (about 7,800 km of track), run by the Ministry of Railways; it carries passengers and goods across the country, linking Karachi port with the north. Importance: cheap and safe transport for passengers and heavy goods (coal, wheat, oil, cement, fertiliser); links ports with industries and markets; provides employment to thousands; important for defence and national unity; saves fuel compared with road transport. Performance: it has expanded and introduced new trains, dry ports and freight services, but suffers from losses, old locomotives and coaches, shortage of engines, delays, accidents, corruption and competition from road transport. Reforms such as new locomotives, track upgradation and CPEC's ML-1 project aim to improve it.

items.q2: Make clear the importance of the computer and information technology (IT).
items.q3: د کمپیوټر او معلوماتي ټکنالوژۍ (IT) اهمیت روښانه کړئ.
items.a: The computer and information technology (IT) means the use of computers, software, the internet and telecommunications to store, process and transmit information. Importance: (1) Faster and accurate work in offices, banks and industries; (2) Banking — online banking, ATMs, mobile wallets; (3) E-commerce — buying and selling online; (4) Education — e-learning, online libraries; (5) Health — hospital records, telemedicine; (6) Communication — e-mail, social media, video calls. (7) Employment and exports — software houses, freelancing and IT exports earn foreign exchange; (8) E-government — NADRA, online tax filing, e-challans; (9) Research and planning — data processing; (10) Industry — automation and design; (11) Agriculture — weather and market information. IT is thus essential for economic development.

items.q: محنت کی استعدادِ عمل (Efficiency) کا دارومدار کن باتوں پر ہے؟ (میرپور آزاد کشمیر بورڈ 2009ء)
items.q2: On what things does the efficiency (Efficiency) of labour depend? (Mirpur Azad Kashmir Board 2009)
items.q3: د کار کاري وړتیا (Efficiency) په کومو خبرو پورې اړه لري؟ (میرپور ازاد کشمیر بورډ ۲۰۰۹)
items.a: The efficiency (productivity) of labour depends on: (1) Physical health and strength; (2) Mental ability and intelligence; (3) General and technical education and training; (4) Character — honesty, hard work and discipline; (5) Climate. (6) Wages and incentives — good pay raises efficiency; (7) Working conditions — light, ventilation, safety and working hours; (8) Quality of machines, tools and raw materials; (9) Efficient organisation and management; (10) Job security and social security. (11) Standard of living — food, housing, recreation; (12) Specialisation and division of labour; (13) Hope of promotion; (14) Peaceful industrial relations; (15) Political and economic stability.
items.h: محنت کی استعداد کو متاثر کرنے والے چار عوامل تحریر کریں؟

items.q: محنت کی نقل پذیری (Mobility of labour) بڑھانے والے عوامل بیان کیجئے۔
items.q2: State the factors increasing the mobility of labour (Mobility of labour).
items.q3: د کار د لېږد (Mobility of labour) زیاتوونکي عوامل بیان کړئ.
items.a: Mobility of labour means the ability of workers to move from one place or occupation to another. Factors increasing it: (1) Education and technical training; (2) Better means of transport and communications; (3) Information about jobs (employment exchanges, internet, media). (4) Higher wages and better facilities elsewhere; (5) Industrialisation and urbanisation creating new jobs; (6) Weakening of family ties and caste/social restrictions; (7) Peace and security; (8) Housing facilities in new places; (9) Opportunities of promotion; (10) Government policies encouraging migration (overseas employment).
items.h: محنت کی استعداد کو متاثر کرنے والے چار عوامل تحریر کریں؟

items.q: پاکستان میں جمعیتِ محنت (Labour Force) کے مسائل بیان کیجئے۔
items.q2: State the problems of the labour force (Labour Force) in Pakistan.
items.q3: په پاکستان کې د کاري ځواک (Labour Force) ستونزې بیان کړئ.
items.a: (1) Low literacy and lack of technical skills; (2) Poor health and nutrition, lowering efficiency; (3) Unemployment and disguised unemployment, especially in rural areas; (4) Low wages and poor living standards; (5) Rapid growth of the labour force due to population growth. (6) Child labour and exploitation; (7) Bad working conditions and lack of safety; (8) Weak trade unions and labour disputes; (9) Lack of social security, pensions and health insurance; (10) Immobility due to family ties and lack of information. (11) Brain drain — skilled workers going abroad; (12) Low participation of women; (13) Insufficient training institutes; (14) Inflation reduces real wages; (15) Weak implementation of labour laws.

items.q: پاکستان میں بے روزگاری کی وجوہات کی وضاحت کیجئے۔ (مری پورا آزاد کشمیر بورڈ 2011ء)
items.q2: Explain the causes of unemployment in Pakistan. (Mirpur Azad Kashmir Board 2011)
items.q3: په پاکستان کې د بې‌روزګارۍ لاملونه روښانه کړئ. (میرپور ازاد کشمیر بورډ ۲۰۱۱)
items.a: (1) Rapid population growth — the labour force grows faster than jobs; (2) Slow industrial growth and closure of factories due to energy shortages; (3) Mechanisation of agriculture reducing farm jobs; (4) Defective education system — degrees without skills; (5) Lack of technical and vocational training. (6) Shortage of capital and low investment; (7) Political instability and law-and-order problems discourage investors; (8) Seasonal nature of agriculture; (9) Immobility of labour; (10) Return of workers from abroad; (11) Unequal distribution of land and wealth. (12) Lack of employment planning; (13) Corruption and merit violations in jobs; (14) Low participation of the private sector; (15) Economic slowdown and inflation.

items.q3: په پاکستان کې د روزګار د فرصتونو (Job opportunities) د زیاتولو لپاره حکومت کوم ګامونه پورته کړي؟
items.a: (1) Expansion of public sector development projects (roads, dams, CPEC); (2) Promotion of industries, special economic zones and SMEs through SMEDA; (3) Easy loans for youth — Prime Minister's Youth Loan Scheme, Kamyab Jawan Programme; (4) Microfinance and Khushhali Bank loans for self-employment. (5) Technical and vocational training through TEVTA, NAVTTC and skill development programmes; (6) Overseas employment through the Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment; (7) Development of IT and freelancing; (8) Agricultural development and rural programmes; (9) Housing and construction schemes (Naya Pakistan Housing) which create jobs. (10) Benazir Income Support Programme/Ehsaas for the poor; (11) Encouragement of foreign and private investment; (12) Employment quotas for women and the disabled; (13) Employment exchanges and job portals.

items.q2: Write the functions of a commercial bank.
items.q3: د سوداګریز بانک دندې ولیکئ.
items.a: Primary functions: (1) Accepting deposits — current (demand), saving and fixed deposits; (2) Advancing loans — overdrafts, cash credit, loans and discounting of bills; (3) Credit creation — creating deposits many times the cash reserve. Agency functions: collecting cheques, bills and dividends; paying insurance premiums, bills and taxes on customers' instructions; buying and selling shares and securities; acting as trustee and executor; transferring money through drafts, pay orders and online transfers. General utility functions: lockers for valuables; traveller's cheques and letters of credit; credit and debit cards, ATMs; issuing references about customers' financial standing; dealing in foreign exchange; collecting economic data; financing foreign trade.
items.h: طلب کے دباؤ اور لاگت فشار افراط میں فرق بتائیں؟

items.q: بینکوں کی اقسام بیان کیجئے۔
items.q2: State the kinds of banks.
items.q3: د بانکونو ډولونه بیان کړئ.
items.a: (1) Central bank — controls currency and credit (State Bank of Pakistan); (2) Commercial banks — accept deposits and give short-term loans (HBL, MCB, UBL, NBP); (3) Industrial banks — long-term finance for industry (Industrial Development Bank, PICIC). (4) Agricultural banks — loans to farmers (Zarai Taraqiati Bank); (5) Exchange banks — finance foreign trade and deal in foreign exchange; (6) Savings banks — encourage small savings (Post Office Savings Bank); (7) Co-operative banks — owned by members for cheap credit (Punjab Provincial Co-operative Bank). (8) Investment banks — help companies raise capital through shares; (9) Islamic banks — work on profit-and-loss sharing (Meezan Bank); (10) Housing finance banks (HBFC); (11) Microfinance banks (Khushhali Bank); (12) Scheduled and non-scheduled banks; (13) Specialised banks such as SME Bank.

items.q: تجارتی بینک اعتباری زر کس طرح تخلیق کرتے ہیں؟ (میرپور آزاد کشمیر بورڈ 2009ء)
items.q2: How do commercial banks create credit money? (Mirpur Azad Kashmir Board 2009)
items.q3: سوداګریز بانکونه اعتباري پیسې څنګه پیدا کوي؟ (میرپور ازاد کشمیر بورډ ۲۰۰۹)
items.a: Credit creation: commercial banks create credit (deposit) money by lending out a large part of the cash deposited with them, keeping only a fraction as cash reserve. Every loan becomes a new deposit in the banking system, which can be lent again. Example: cash reserve ratio = 20%. A deposits Rs 1000; the bank keeps Rs 200 and lends Rs 800. The Rs 800 is deposited in a bank, which keeps Rs 160 and lends Rs 640, and so on: 1000 + 800 + 640 + 512 + … = Rs 5000. Formula: Credit money = Original deposit ÷ Cash reserve ratio = 1000 ÷ 0.20 = Rs 5000; credit created = 5000 − 1000 = Rs 4000. Limits: the cash reserve ratio, amount of cash in the economy, demand for loans, availability of securities, business conditions, the monetary policy of the central bank, and people's banking habits.
items.h: طلب کے دباؤ اور لاگت فشار افراط میں فرق بتائیں؟

items.q: افراطِ زر کے عمومی اسباب بیان کیجئے۔
items.q2: State the general causes of inflation.
items.q3: د انفلاسیون عمومي لاملونه بیان کړئ.
items.a: Inflation is a persistent rise in the general price level. Causes on the demand side (demand-pull): (1) Increase in money supply — printing notes, deficit financing; (2) Increase in bank credit; (3) Rise in incomes and spending; (4) Increase in government expenditure; (5) Population growth; (6) Black money and hoarding. Causes on the supply side (cost-push): (1) Fall in production because of floods, droughts or energy shortages; (2) Rise in costs — wages, raw materials, fuel prices; (3) Indirect taxes raise prices; (4) Devaluation of currency making imports dearer; (5) Monopolies and profiteering; (6) Imported inflation from world prices; (7) Smuggling and black marketing.
items.h: طلب کے دباؤ اور لاگت فشار افراط میں فرق بتائیں؟

items.q: پاکستان میں افراطِ زر کے اسباب بیان کریں۔ (بہاولپور بورڈ 2011ء)
items.q2: State the causes of inflation in Pakistan. (Bahawalpur Board 2011)
items.q3: په پاکستان کې د انفلاسیون لاملونه بیان کړئ. (بهاولپور بورډ ۲۰۱۱)
items.a: (1) Deficit financing and borrowing from the State Bank; (2) Rapid increase in money supply and bank credit; (3) Rising oil prices and electricity/gas tariffs; (4) Devaluation of the rupee raising import costs; (5) Increase in indirect taxes (GST, excise). (6) Fall in agricultural production due to floods, droughts and pests; (7) Population growth increasing demand; (8) Hoarding, smuggling and profiteering by traders; (9) Heavy non-development expenditure (defence, debt servicing); (10) Wage increases without productivity growth. (11) Home remittances and black money increasing spending; (12) Weak price control machinery; (13) Imported inflation — high world prices of edible oil and food; (14) Energy shortages reducing industrial output.
items.h: طلب کے دباؤ اور لاگت فشار افراط میں فرق بتائیں؟

items.q: پاکستان میں رائج افراطِ زر کا علاج بتائیے۔ اس ضمن میں حکومت نے کون کون سے اقدامات کئے ہیں؟
items.q2: State the remedy of the inflation prevalent in Pakistan. In this connection which measures has the government taken?
items.q3: په پاکستان کې د رواج انفلاسیون درملنه ووایاست. په دې برخه کې حکومت کوم ګامونه پورته کړي؟
items.a: Remedies: Monetary measures — raise interest rate (policy rate), raise cash reserve ratio, open market sales of securities, selective credit control; Fiscal measures — cut unnecessary government expenditure, avoid deficit financing, increase direct taxes, reduce indirect taxes on necessities. Other measures — increase production of agriculture and industry; import scarce goods; control hoarding and smuggling; effective price control; rationing of essential goods; stop wage increases not linked to productivity; reduce population growth. Government steps: the State Bank tightened monetary policy (higher policy rate); restrictions on borrowing from the State Bank; Utility Stores selling goods at subsidised rates; targeted subsidies (BISP/Ehsaas); price control committees and market magistrates; imports of wheat, sugar and edible oil to stabilise prices; agreements with the IMF to reduce the budget deficit.
items.h: طلب کے دباؤ اور لاگت فشار افراط میں فرق بتائیں؟

items.q: افراطِ زر کے اثرات تحریر کریں۔ (ملتان بورڈ 2009ء)
items.q2: Write the effects of inflation. (Multan Board 2009)
items.q3: د انفلاسیون اغېزې ولیکئ. (ملتان بورډ ۲۰۰۹)
items.a: Effects on production: mild inflation raises profits and encourages investment and output, but high inflation creates uncertainty and discourages long-term investment. Effects on distribution: (1) Fixed-income groups (salaried, pensioners, labourers) lose as real income falls; (2) Businessmen, traders and producers gain; (3) Debtors gain, creditors lose; (4) Farmers may gain from higher crop prices; (5) Inequalities of income increase. Other effects: savings fall as money loses value; people buy property and gold; exports become expensive and imports rise, worsening the balance of payments; the value of the currency falls; corruption, hoarding and black marketing increase; social unrest and strikes; government expenditure increases.

items.q: نیشنل بینک آف پاکستان پر ایک نوٹ لکھیے۔
items.q2: Write a note on the National Bank of Pakistan.
items.q3: د پاکستان پر ملي بانک یادښت ولیکئ.
items.a: The National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) was established in November 1949 to finance the jute trade during the crisis with India; it is the largest commercial bank in the public sector, with branches throughout Pakistan and abroad. Functions: (1) Agent of the State Bank where the SBP has no branch — handles government receipts and payments, treasury operations and collection of taxes; (2) Accepts deposits and gives loans like other commercial banks; (3) Finances agriculture, industry, trade and exports; (4) Pays government salaries and pensions. (5) Deals in foreign exchange and remittances; (6) Handles public debt and government securities; (7) Provides utility bill collection, lockers and modern banking (ATMs, online); (8) Gives loans for small businesses and housing; (9) Plays a role in national development schemes.

items.q: زرعی ترقیاتی بینک لمیٹڈ (ZTBL) کے فرائض بیان کیجئے۔
items.q2: State the functions of Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited (ZTBL).
items.q3: د زرعي ترقیاتي بانک لمیټډ (ZTBL) دندې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited (ZTBL), formerly the Agricultural Development Bank of Pakistan (established in 1961), is a specialised bank for agricultural credit. Functions: (1) Gives short-, medium- and long-term loans to farmers for seeds, fertilisers, pesticides, tractors, tubewells and machinery; (2) Loans for livestock, dairy, poultry, fisheries and orchards; (3) Loans for land development, farm buildings and storage; (4) Easy and interest-subsidised credit for small farmers; (5) Loans for cottage and agro-based industries in rural areas. (6) Technical guidance through mobile credit officers; (7) Accepts deposits to mobilise rural savings; (8) Crop insurance schemes; (9) Helps to raise agricultural productivity and rural income and reduce dependence on moneylenders.

items.q: سٹیٹ بینک آف پاکستان کے فرائض بیان کیجئے۔ (میرپور آزاد کشمیر بورڈ 2011ء)
items.q2: State the functions of the State Bank of Pakistan. (Mirpur Azad Kashmir Board 2011)
items.q3: د پاکستان دولتي بانک دندې بیان کړئ. (میرپور ازاد کشمیر بورډ ۲۰۱۱)
items.a: The State Bank of Pakistan (established 1 July 1948) is the central bank. Functions: (1) Issue of currency notes — sole right of note issue; (2) Banker, agent and adviser to the government — keeps government accounts, manages public debt, gives loans and economic advice. (3) Bankers' bank — commercial banks keep cash reserves with it; it supervises and regulates them; (4) Lender of last resort — rediscounts bills and lends to banks in crisis; (5) Clearing house — settles inter-bank claims; (6) Controller of credit — uses bank rate, open market operations, cash reserve ratio and selective controls (monetary policy). (7) Custodian of foreign exchange reserves and manages the exchange rate; (8) Promotional functions — development of the banking system, agricultural and industrial credit, Islamic banking; (9) Collects and publishes economic statistics and reports; (10) Maintains price stability and promotes economic growth; (11) Relations with international institutions such as the IMF.

items.q: مرکزی حکومت پاکستان کی آمدنی کے ذرائع بیان کریں۔
items.q2: State the sources of income of the central government of Pakistan.
items.q3: د پاکستان د مرکزي حکومت د عاید سرچینې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Tax revenue: (1) Income tax and corporation tax — the largest direct tax; (2) Sales tax/General Sales Tax (GST) — the largest single source; (3) Customs duties on imports and exports; (4) Federal excise duty on industrial goods and services; (5) Capital value tax, withholding taxes, petroleum levy. Non-tax revenue: (1) Profits of the State Bank and public enterprises (PTCL, OGDCL, PIA dividends); (2) Interest on loans to provinces and public corporations; (3) Fees, fines and charges — passports, licences, telecom licences; (4) Income of railways and post offices; (5) Gas development surcharge and royalties on oil and gas. Capital receipts: internal borrowing (national savings schemes, treasury bills, Pakistan Investment Bonds), external loans and grants (IMF, World Bank, ADB, friendly countries), privatisation proceeds, and deficit financing.

items.q: پاکستان کے نظامِ محصولات کا جائزہ لیجئے۔
items.q2: Take a review of the tax system of Pakistan.
items.q3: د پاکستان د مالیاتي نظام ارزونه وکړئ.
items.a: Pakistan's tax system: federal taxes (income tax, sales tax, customs, federal excise) are collected by the Federal Board of Revenue; provinces collect agricultural income tax, property tax, stamp duty, motor vehicle tax, sales tax on services and abiana. Features/weaknesses: (1) Narrow tax base — a very small part of the population files returns; (2) Low tax-to-GDP ratio (about 9–11%); (3) Heavy reliance on indirect taxes (about 60–70%), which is regressive; (4) Large-scale tax evasion and undocumented economy; (5) Exemptions for influential sectors; (6) Agriculture and retail trade are under-taxed. (7) Complicated and frequently changing laws; (8) Weak administration and corruption; (9) Withholding taxes form a large part of direct taxes; (10) Reforms — GST, universal self-assessment, computerisation, NTN registration and the Active Taxpayers List — have been introduced but more improvement is needed.

items.q: پاکستان کے محصولاتی نظام کو بہتر بنانے کے لئے تجاویز پیش کریں۔
items.q2: Present proposals for making the revenue system of Pakistan better.
items.q3: د پاکستان د محصولاتي نظام د ښه کولو لپاره وړاندیزونه وړاندې کړئ.
items.a: (1) Widen the tax base by bringing all earners, including big landlords, traders and professionals, into the tax net; (2) Use NADRA and bank data to identify non-filers; (3) Reduce dependence on indirect taxes and increase the share of direct taxes; (4) Simplify the laws and make them stable; reduce rates but remove exemptions. (5) Computerise and automate tax administration; e-filing and e-payment; (6) Train and adequately pay tax officials; strict accountability for corruption; (7) Document the economy — encourage banking transactions and discourage cash dealings; (8) Develop a tax culture by awareness campaigns and by spending revenue honestly on public services. (9) Increase non-tax revenue through efficient public enterprises; (10) Control smuggling and under-invoicing; (11) Collect zakat and ushr efficiently; (12) Reduce wasteful expenditure so that taxes are not raised; (13) Improve coordination between federal and provincial revenue authorities.

items.q: مرکزی حکومت کی مالیاتی پالیسی (Fiscal Policy) کے بڑے بڑے مقاصد بیان کیجئے۔
items.q2: State the big objectives of the fiscal policy (Fiscal Policy) of the central government.
items.q3: د مرکزي حکومت د مالي پالیسۍ (Fiscal Policy) لویې موخې بیان کړئ.
items.a: (1) Mobilisation of resources — raising revenue for development and public services; (2) Economic growth — encouraging saving, investment and production through tax concessions and development spending; (3) Full employment — public works and incentives to industry. (4) Price stability — controlling inflation and deflation through taxes, expenditure and borrowing; (5) Fair distribution of income and wealth — progressive taxes and spending on the poor; (6) Balance of payments improvement — import duties, export rebates. (7) Reduction of the budget deficit and public debt; (8) Development of backward regions; (9) Provision of social services — education, health, housing; (10) Allocation of resources to priority sectors; (11) Establishment of a welfare state.

items.q: پاکستان کی صوبائی حکومتوں کے ذرائع آمدنی پر بحث کریں۔ (میرپور آزاد کشمیر بورڈ 2010ء، ملتان بورڈ 2011ء)
items.q2: Discuss the sources of income of the provincial governments of Pakistan. (Mirpur Azad Kashmir Board 2010, Multan Board 2011)
items.q3: د پاکستان د ولایتي حکومتونو د عاید پر سرچینو بحث وکړئ. (میرپور ازاد کشمیر بورډ ۲۰۱۰، ملتان بورډ ۲۰۱۱)
items.a: (1) Share in the federal divisible pool under the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award — the biggest source (more than 80% of provincial revenue), distributed mainly on the basis of population; (2) Straight transfers — royalties and development surcharges on oil and gas, excise on natural gas; (3) Grants and special grants from the federal government. Provincial taxes: agricultural income tax, land revenue, property tax (urban immovable property), stamp duty and registration fees, motor vehicle tax, provincial excise (on liquor, etc.), entertainment tax, professional tax, sales tax on services (collected by PRA, SRB, KPRA, BRA), abiana (water rate), electricity duty. Non-tax sources: fees of courts and educational institutions, income from forests, irrigation, provincial public enterprises, fines, and loans from the federal government and foreign agencies.

items.q: زکوٰۃ کے مستحقین کون کون ہیں؟
items.q2: Who are the recipients of zakat?
items.q3: د زکات مستحقین څوک دي؟
items.a: The recipients of zakat are named in the Holy Quran (At-Taubah 9:60) — eight categories: (1) Fuqara — the poor who have little; (2) Masakin — the needy who have nothing; (3) Amileen — those employed to collect and distribute zakat; (4) Muallafat-ul-Quloob — those whose hearts are to be reconciled (new Muslims). (5) Fir-riqab — freeing slaves and captives; (6) Al-gharimeen — debtors unable to pay their debts; (7) Fi sabeelillah — in the way of Allah (jihad, religious and welfare purposes); (8) Ibn-us-sabeel — travellers in need, away from home.

items.q: زکوٰۃ کی معاشی اور معاشرتی اہمیت پر نوٹ لکھیں۔ (بہاولپور بورڈ 2011ء)
items.q2: Write a note on the economic and social importance of zakat. (Bahawalpur Board 2011)
items.q3: د زکات پر اقتصادي او ټولنیز اهمیت یادښت ولیکئ. (بهاولپور بورډ ۲۰۱۱)
items.a: Economic importance: (1) Circulation of wealth — it prevents concentration of wealth in a few hands; (2) Reduces poverty and inequality by transferring wealth from the rich to the poor; (3) Discourages hoarding — idle wealth decreases each year by 2.5%, so it is invested; (4) Increases investment, production and employment. (5) Increases demand — the poor spend zakat on necessities, which expands markets; (6) Social security — help for orphans, widows, disabled, unemployed and debtors; (7) Reduces the government's burden of welfare expenditure; (8) Encourages lawful earning and economic stability. Social importance: purifies wealth and the soul from greed and miserliness; creates brotherhood, love and cooperation between rich and poor; reduces crime, jealousy and class conflict; makes society stable and peaceful; and establishes an Islamic welfare state. In Pakistan zakat and ushr are collected under the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance 1980.

items.a: (1) Persistent deficit — imports exceed exports; (2) Exports concentrated on a few items — cotton, textiles, rice, leather, sports and surgical goods; (3) Imports mainly of petroleum, machinery, chemicals, edible oil, vehicles and iron and steel. (4) Shift from raw materials to manufactured exports; (5) Concentration of markets — USA, EU, China, UAE, Afghanistan; (6) Low value-added and low-quality exports; (7) Exports affected by world prices and quotas; (8) Most trade is by sea through Karachi and Port Qasim. (9) Rising import bill due to oil prices and population growth; (10) Government's control through tariffs, licences and export incentives; (11) Growing trade with China under CPEC and free-trade agreements; (12) Dependence on remittances and loans to finance the trade deficit.

items.a: (1) Increase production of exportable goods — modern agriculture and industry; (2) Improve quality and standardisation to meet international standards; (3) Diversify exports — new products (IT, engineering goods, pharmaceuticals) and value addition to cotton. (4) Find new markets — Africa, Central Asia, Latin America; trade agreements; (5) Reduce cost of production — cheap energy, modern machinery, skilled labour; (6) Export incentives — rebates, tax refunds, cheap export finance; (7) Trade fairs, exhibitions and commercial attachés abroad. (8) Simplify export procedures; one-window facility; (9) Stable and realistic exchange rate; (10) Improve infrastructure — ports, roads, dry ports, cold storage; (11) Control smuggling; (12) Political stability and good law and order; (13) Encourage foreign investment in export industries; (14) Develop SMEs and the export of services and IT.

items.a: (1) Imports far exceed exports — large trade deficit; (2) Rising oil import bill; (3) Narrow export base dependent on textiles; (4) Low quality and high cost of exports; (5) Fall in world prices of our exports. (6) Heavy repayment of foreign loans and interest; (7) Import of luxury goods; (8) Rapid population growth increasing demand for imports; (9) Energy shortages reducing exports; (10) Political instability and law-and-order problems; (11) Protectionism by developed countries. (12) Natural disasters damaging export crops; (13) Decline in foreign investment and aid at times; (14) Smuggling and under-invoicing; (15) Devaluation raising the cost of imports and debt.

items.a: (1) Increase exports through higher production, diversification, quality improvement and new markets; (2) Reduce unnecessary imports — high duties on luxury goods; (3) Import substitution — produce at home goods now imported (edible oil, machinery); (4) Develop local energy resources (hydel, coal, solar) to cut the oil bill. (11) Population control; (12) Austerity in government expenditure; (13) Trade agreements with neighbouring countries; (14) Political stability and good governance; (15) Development of IT and services exports.

items.q: سارک ممالک (SAARC) کے اہم مقاصد بیان کیجئے۔
items.q2: State the important objectives of SAARC countries (SAARC).
items.q3: د سارک هېوادونو (SAARC) مهمې موخې بیان کړئ.
items.a: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was founded in Dhaka in December 1985; its secretariat is in Kathmandu. Members: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan (since 2007). Objectives: (1) Promote the welfare and quality of life of the people of South Asia; (2) Accelerate economic growth, social progress and cultural development; (3) Promote self-reliance among member countries; (4) Mutual trust and understanding; (5) Cooperation in agriculture, trade, science, technology, transport, health and education. (6) Expansion of regional trade — SAPTA (1995) and SAFTA (2006); (7) Cooperation with other developing countries and international organisations; (8) Joint efforts against poverty, terrorism, drugs and natural disasters; (9) Strengthen cooperation in international forums on common interests.
